sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 07-02-2024 at about 11.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-KK-3598, by wearing helmet, slowly, cautiously, by observing all the traffic rules and norms.

When he reached near Madduramma Temple, Huskur Village, Sarjapura Hobli, Bengaluru, a Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1747, came in a high speed, in rash and negligent manner, in reverse mode and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Al-Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as employee at private company and was earning a sum of Rs.17,000/- per month.

But, due to the accidental injuries,
he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Hebbagodi Police have registered the case against the driver of the said lorry, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tata Ace bearing No.KA-51-B-1747 in favour of respondent No.2 and its validity as on the date of accident.

Further it is contended that,
the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the insured vehicle as on the date of accident.
Thereby the owner of the vehicle has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, no accident as stated in the claim petition has taken place, there was no Deepak Kumar H vs Royal Sun Ins Co Ltd on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96732654/
2 negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata ace bearing Reg. No.KA-51- B-1747 and the petitioner has not sustained any injuries in the alleged accident, as stated in the claim petition and there is no nexus between injuries sustained to the petitioner and alleged accident.

sentences.text: The alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the petitioner himself and he has dashed his motorcycle to the insured Tata Ace vehicle of the respondent No.2, parked on the left side of the road, infront of Huskur market, by following the traffic rules.

At the time of alleged accident, the driver of Tata Ace vehicle was delivering office materials, meanwhile the petitioner speaking in his mobile, carelessly came and dashed against the Tata Ace vehicle of the respondent No.2, from behind and fell down.
But, to get unlawful gain, the petitioner has lodged a false complaint and false petition against the respondent No.1.
Hence, the above claim petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1747 was not possessing valid fitness certificate and permit to ply the said vehicle on the road.
As such, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and rules and regulations of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismiss the petition.

No.KA-51- B-1747 ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1747 in a reverse direction and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his left leg and other parts of the body.

sentences.text: In order to establish the above contentions, the respondent No.1 insurance company has examined its authorised person/investigator incharge officer.

The R.W.1 has deposed in her examination-in-chief affidavit that, on procuring and verification of crime records obtained from the concerned hospital authority by their independent investigator, they have noted that, the alleged Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.Ka-51-B-1747 was not at all involved in the alleged accident, as per the initial hospital records and MLC extract of Al-Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein the history of accident is clearly stated that, "H/o RTA from a 4 wheeler Tempo with registration No.KA-51-B- 1746."

On verification of vehicle history report of vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1746 is revealed that, the same vehicle is also a Tata Ace vehicle and the same was not having valid insurance policy, as on the date of accident.
Hence, the petitioner to get unlawful gain has falsely implicated the insured Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.Ka- 51-B-1747, which was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

In support of her oral evidence, the R.W.1 has produced the MLC register extract of Al-Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru, which is marked as Ex.R.3 and the 'B' Register extract and Vehicle History Report pertaining to Tata Ace Vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-510B-1746.

No doubt, as rightly contended by the respondent No.1, as per the entry made in the column 'history of accident of injury' in Ex.R.3 MLC register extract of Al-Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru, the road traffic accident is caused by a four wheeler Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-1746, at Electronic City, near SRS Brundhavana Pharmacy Hospital, on 07-02-2024, at around 11:40 a.m.

But, it is pertinent to note that, nowhere in the said register the name of informant, who has given the said information about the history of accident to the hospital authorities, has been mentioned.
It is just mentioned that, the patient was brought to the hospital by his parents.

Further is pertinent to note that, in the said column it is clearly mentioned that, the patient had sustained injury on his left foot and after the accident he was taken first to SRS Brundhavana Pharma Hospital, wherein primary aid is given to the petitioner and from there the petitioner was taken to Al-Ameen Hospital for further treatment, at 2:00 p.m., on 07-02-2024.
It is not the case of the respondent No.1 that, the parents of petitioner were the eye-witness to the alleged accident.

In such circumstances, the history of road traffic accident recorded in the SRS Brundhavana Pharma Hospital, Bengaluru, where the petitioner was taken immediately after the accident and he had been provided first aid treatment, is more relevant than the history of road traffic accident recorded in Al-Ameen Hospital, wherein the petitioner was taken for further treatment.
But, the respondent No.1 has not produced any document pertaining to SRS Brundhavana Pharma Hospital, Bengaluru.

Non -production of said documents by the respondent No.1, leads this Court to draw adverse inference against the respondent No.1 and hold that, the respondent No.1 by taking undue advantage of the wrong vehicle number mentioned in Ex.R.3 MLC register extract of Al-Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru, has taken false defence in the case, contending that, the Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-1747 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the same has been falsely implicated by the petitioner, instead of Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-B-1746.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, the respondent No.1 has not examined the author of the Ex.R.3 MLC register extract, to prove the contents of said documents.
It is settled principle of law that, mere production and marking of a document in the evidence does not constitute proof of its contents.

Therefore, except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, there is Deepak Kumar H vs Royal Sun Ins Co Ltd on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96732654/
5 no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself and the offending Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-1747 was not at all involved in the said accident.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1747 in a reverse direction and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, which was proceeding in the same direction and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left leg and other parts of the body in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of the road, near Madduramma Temple, Huskur Village, Sarjapura Hobli,
Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District, in between the offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B- 1747 and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-KK-3598 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge- sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1747 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1747.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 discharge summary,
Ex.P.11 x-ray and Ex.P.12 clinical report, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained left Type II B compound fracture of the shaft of the 2nd and 3rd metatarsal and tendon injury of the 2nd and 3rd extensor digitorum longus tendon.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Deepak Kumar H vs Royal Sun Ins Co Ltd on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96732654/

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 07-02-2024 at about 11:30 a.m., near Madduramma Temple, Huskur Village, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-B-1747. Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1747 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained left Type II B compound fracture of the shaft of the 2nd and 3rd metatarsal and tendon injury of the 2 nd and 3rd extensor digitorum longus tendon and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his driving licence, which is marked as Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the date of birth of the petitioner is 06-06-1992.
The accident has taken place on 07-02-2024 at about 11:30 a.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 32 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered left Type II B compound fracture of the shaft of the 2nd and 3rd metatarsal and tendon Deepak Kumar H vs Royal Sun Ins Co Ltd on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96732654/
7 injury of the 2 nd and 3rd extensor digitorum longus tendon.

sentences.text: Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 30% physical disability of left lower limb and 10% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.5 wound certificate,
Ex.P.8 discharge summary, Ex.P.11 x-ray and Ex.P.12 clinical report clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, the accident has occurred on 07-02-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 11-02-2025, which is after lapse of one year from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further, he has deposed that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after removal of all implants, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, he has assessed only physical disability of the petitioner and not functional disability, fracture is united with implants in situ, the petitioner can perform day to day activities with some difficulties and the range of movements of hip and knee are normal.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 7% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as employee at private company and was earning a sum of Rs.17,000/- per month.

Further, he has deposed that,
due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, he has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as employee at private company and was earning a sum of Rs.17,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2024.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 32 years is 16.

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,98,000 X 7/100 X 16 = Rs.2,21,760/-.

sentences.text: Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 20 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.93,944/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.93,944/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. left Type II B compound fracture of the shaft of the 2nd and 3rd metatarsal and tendon injury of the 2nd and 3rd extensor digitorum longus tendon.

As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days from 07-02-2024 to 09-02-2024, in Al-Ameen Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore,
taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days in Al-Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent some amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 3 = Rs.3,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 3 days in Al-Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent some amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 3 = Rs.2,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of G.K. Layout, Parappana Agrahara,
Electronic City, Bengaluru, the accident has occurred near Madduramma Temple, Huskur Village,
Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District and he has taken treatment at Al-Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places

,
compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 3 days as in-patient at Al- Ameen Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.16,500 x 2 = Rs.33,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 32 years and unfortunately he has suffered left Type II B compound fracture of the shaft of the 2nd and 3rd metatarsal and tendon injury of the 2 nd and 3rd extensor digitorum longus tendon.

Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 7%
to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.

20. Liability : Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B- 1747.
As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 bearing No.VGC0931014000100, in respect of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B- 1747, was valid from 01-04-2023 to 31-03-2024.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-1747 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
